title: Wire the SkinnedMeshRenderer adapter into the live runtime/editor preview path for a demonstrable idle/walk
description:
## Summary
TSK-0132 validated the CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer adapter via PlayMode tests, but rg confirms CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind is called ONLY from its test file. CreatureRuntimePreview still attaches static MeshFilter/MeshRenderer per item (unrelated to CreatureRig). No live path renders a real generated creature through a SkinnedMeshRenderer, so the animation-MVP's user-visible idle/walk is not yet demonstrable in the running editor/game. This is the integration step that turns the validated SMR-vs-LBS MVP gate into a visible feature.

## User Mandate
STRICT
- Fixed point: current main head in this workspace; this is sequential round 3 of a 5-round sprint and the source tree is the source of truth.
- Owning task: TSK-0142 — Wire the SkinnedMeshRenderer adapter into the live runtime/editor preview path for a demonstrable idle/walk.
- Acceptance criteria: A real generated creature renders through a SkinnedMeshRenderer in the running preview with an idle pose applied, no per-frame mesh/weight/bindpose rebuild. Teardown leaves no orphaned objects; source mesh remains unmodified.
- Scope and stop boundary: Only touch the live preview/runtime integration for the SkinnedMeshRenderer presentation path. Keep runtime/editor ownership clean; runtime presenter does not acquire editor-API/session state. Do not broaden into locomotion frameworks, generic animation infrastructure, or TSK-0130/0134 work. Do not commit or push.
- Hypothesis: The existing validated adapter can be attached to the live runtime preview path without reintroducing per-frame mesh rebuilds, once the pose boundary and morphology radius bridge are in place.
- Discriminating check: In the runtime preview, a real generated creature should render through a SkinnedMeshRenderer and update under an idle pose without reauthoring weights/bindposes per frame.
- Validation gate: dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore; dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore; focused PlayMode preview smoke test for live adapter integration; git diff --check.
- Repo contract: Runtime under Assets/Scripts/Runtime has no scene-object/editor dependency. The preview integration is the presentation layer only; generation stays pose-free. Keep the implementation minimal and follow the existing adapter contract from TSK-0132.
- Required report format: Owning task key; Changed files; Exact commands + results; What passed / did not pass / blockers; Residual risk and next step; Non-obvious design decisions explicitly called out.

## Scope
- Wire CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer into the live presentation/preview path (a real generated creature rendered via SkinnedMeshRenderer whose semantic skeleton is driven by an authored/idle pose), consuming the TSK-0131 weights + radius bridge and the CreatureRig indexed bones.
- Sequence behind TSK-0133 (external pose-driver decision + minimal harness) and the morphology-radius bridge; use the minimal authored-pose test/demo driver, NOT a locomotion framework (external rig out of scope).
- Keep runtime/editor ownership clean: runtime presenter does not acquire editor-API/session state; editor preview owns the integration lifecycle. GeneratedCreature stays pose-free.
- Do not build TSK-0130 rigid weighting or TSK-0134 budget here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A real generated creature renders through a SkinnedMeshRenderer in the running preview with an idle pose applied, no per-frame mesh/weight/bindpose rebuild, zero managed alloc on pose ticks.
- Teardown leaves no orphaned objects; source mesh unmodified.

## Validation
PlayMode (real GeneratedCreature via preview path) + relevant Editor preview smoke; dotnet builds; git diff --check.
